page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.2xlarge is an x86_64 architecture server instance belonging to the ecs.e family. Powered by an Intel Xeon CPU running at 2.5 GHz, this instance features 8 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core under a shared CPU allocation model. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing 2.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard operations. The instance achieves a stress-ng single-core score of 1729.79 and a multi-core score of 7072.24. Passmark CPU and memory scores are also in the average tier, with a CPU score of 11140.77 and a database operations score of 4207.46. However, single-threaded compression and decompression tasks show performance limitations, with gzip compression scoring in the bottom 10% at 18.66 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression scoring in the bottom 25% at 22.75 GB/sec.

Given its shared CPU allocation and lack of bundled local storage, this instance offers a cost-effective option for workloads that require multiple vCPUs but do not demand sustained, dedicated CPU performance. It is suitable for entry-level web serving, Redis caching, and moderate database operations that can tolerate shared resource environments.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e-c1m2.2xlarge is an x86_64 server instance within the ecs.e family, utilizing a KVM hypervisor. It features 8 vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it operates on a shared CPU allocation model with 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Performance benchmarks place this server in the average tier for most tasks, including a Passmark CPU score of 11140.77 and Redis SET throughput of 9.25 million operations per second, though single-threaded compression performance is weak. Given its resource density and shared CPU architecture, it represents a budget-friendly option for non-critical workloads. It is best suited for static web serving, Redis caching, and lightweight database operations.
